scenes.tts: How can one human choice make one river population rise while another falls? Watch one Virginia river as people change who lives there and what each population can use.
scenes.caption: How can one human choice make one river population rise while another falls? Watch one Virginia river as people change who lives there and what each population can use.
scenes.visual: Build the carried world immediately in a full 16:9 river cross-section filling at least 70% of frame height. COLOUR MAP for both films: introduced blue catfish BLUE; native white catfish GOLD; crabs, small fish and shared prey TEAL; healthy shoreline habitat GREEN; human pressures RED; other labels WHITE. Slow water flow and waving marsh grass never stop. A BLUE release arrow enters from a human hand on shore. Two population bars at right move in opposite directions, both labelled 'schematic'. The question appears over the water, not on a separate title card.
scenes.narration: How can one human choice make one river population rise while another falls? Watch one Virginia river as people change who lives there and what each population can use.

scenes.visual: Keep water, fish and marsh moving behind a two-second title overlay, 'One Change, Many Ripples'. The title dissolves back into the same river; no cut to a blank frame.

scenes.tts: Start with one river edge. Green marsh plants provide habitat along the bank. Teal crabs and small fish move below. Gold white catfish are native here. All the white catfish in this river form one population. The shoreline shelters animals while the moving water carries food.
scenes.caption: Start with one river edge. Green marsh plants provide habitat along the bank. Teal crabs and small fish move below. Gold white catfish are native here. All the white catfish in this river form one population. The shoreline shelters animals while the moving water carries food.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the same river until marsh, bottom and open water fill the frame. GREEN roots grow downward as TEAL crabs shelter among them. A loose school of TEAL small fish crosses the current. Three GOLD white catfish swim together; a bracket labelled 'one population: white catfish' gathers them without freezing their motion.
scenes.narration: Start with one river edge. Green marsh plants provide habitat along the bank. Teal crabs and small fish move below. Gold white catfish are native here. All the white catfish in this river form one population. The shoreline shelters animals while the moving water carries food.

scenes.tts: People belong inside this ecosystem, too. They depend on it for food, water, energy and other resources. Their choices can change habitat, available resources, or which species are present. A habitat is where an organism finds the food, water and shelter it needs.
scenes.caption: People belong inside this ecosystem, too. They depend on it for food, water, energy and other resources. Their choices can change habitat, available resources, or which species are present. A habitat is where an organism finds the food, water and shelter it needs.
scenes.visual: Pull upward but retain the underwater world. On the bank, a person draws water, another holds a fish basket and a small home lights up. Three thin arrows lead back to the river, labelled 'water', 'food' and 'energy'. A GREEN outline closes around roots, water and prey, then becomes a large label: 'habitat = needs met here'.
scenes.narration: People belong inside this ecosystem, too. They depend on it for food, water, energy and other resources. Their choices can change habitat, available resources, or which species are present. A habitat is where an organism finds the food, water and shelter it needs.

scenes.tts: Now people release blue catfish, shown in blue. These fish came from waters outside Virginia's Bay rivers. Here they spread and cause harm, so they are invasive, not merely new. Being new is not enough.
scenes.caption: Now people release blue catfish, shown in blue. These fish came from waters outside Virginia's Bay rivers. Here they spread and cause harm, so they are invasive, not merely new. Being new is not enough.
scenes.visual: A bucket at the bank tips and one BLUE catfish enters the carried river. It becomes several as a BLUE population bar grows, labelled 'schematic'. Beside it, three large stepping stones light in sequence: 'brought here', 'spreads', 'causes harm'. Only after all three glow does the word 'invasive' appear.
scenes.narration: Now people release blue catfish, shown in blue. These fish came from waters outside Virginia's Bay rivers. Here they spread and cause harm, so they are invasive, not merely new. Being new is not enough.

scenes.tts: Blue catfish eat plants and animals, including fish and sometimes blue crabs. Scientists report that white catfish eat similar prey. When species need the same limited resource, they may compete, even without a fight. One fish can simply eat food another fish needed.
scenes.caption: Blue catfish eat plants and animals, including fish and sometimes blue crabs. Scientists report that white catfish eat similar prey. When species need the same limited resource, they may compete, even without a fight. One fish can simply eat food another fish needed.
scenes.visual: Transform the river bottom into a close view while keeping the same colours and current. A central TEAL prey pool contains moving small fish and crabs. Curved arrows extend from both BLUE and GOLD catfish toward that one pool. No attack or fight is shown. The pool gently refills, but feeding removes items faster. Add a small 'schematic' label.
scenes.narration: Blue catfish eat plants and animals, including fish and sometimes blue crabs. Scientists report that white catfish eat similar prey. When species need the same limited resource, they may compete, even without a fight. One fish can simply eat food another fish needed.

scenes.tts: Both catfish now use the teal prey pool. If the blue population grows, what do you predict happens to the food remaining for white catfish?
scenes.caption: Both catfish now use the teal prey pool. If the blue population grows, what do you predict happens to the food remaining for white catfish?
scenes.visual: Keep the shared TEAL pool centered and large. The BLUE population bar begins rising but pauses halfway. The GOLD catfish waits on the opposite side. Place the question above the pool in WHITE. All feeding arrows stop at their starting points while water particles drift.
scenes.narration: Both catfish now use the teal prey pool. If the blue population grows, what do you predict happens to the food remaining for white catfish?

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Hold the same question and half-raised BLUE bar. Water and prey drift slowly, but no answer appears and no food is removed.

scenes.tts: More blue catfish feed, and the shared prey pool may shrink. Less food may remain for white catfish. That is a possible competition pathway, not proof of what caused a real population change. Other habitat changes may matter at the same time.
scenes.caption: More blue catfish feed, and the shared prey pool may shrink. Less food may remain for white catfish. That is a possible competition pathway, not proof of what caused a real population change. Other habitat changes may matter at the same time.
scenes.visual: Release the paused motion. The BLUE bar rises and several BLUE fish feed. The TEAL pool shrinks but does not vanish; the word 'may' stays beside its downward arrow. The GOLD fish finds fewer prey. A dotted bracket labels this path 'possible', while faint RED question-mark arrows from shore remain visible as other possible changes.
scenes.narration: More blue catfish feed, and the shared prey pool may shrink. Less food may remain for white catfish. That is a possible competition pathway, not proof of what caused a real population change. Other habitat changes may matter at the same time.

scenes.tts: People also fill part of the green marsh for homes. Habitat disappears, so some animals must move or die. Runoff enters the water, and extra fertilizer can later lower oxygen. Both changes may affect several local populations.
scenes.caption: People also fill part of the green marsh for homes. Habitat disappears, so some animals must move or die. Runoff enters the water, and extra fertilizer can later lower oxygen. Both changes may affect several local populations.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole carried river. A RED construction block slides over half the GREEN marsh; sheltered TEAL animals move away in different directions. A RED runoff ribbon flows from a field into the current. An oxygen gauge appears, explicitly labelled 'schematic', and may drift downward later without reaching zero.
scenes.narration: People also fill part of the green marsh for homes. Habitat disappears, so some animals must move or die. Runoff enters the water, and extra fertilizer can later lower oxygen. Both changes may affect several local populations.

scenes.tts: Watch the whole river, not one arrow. Blue catfish rise. Shared prey and shoreline habitat change. Crabs, small fish and white catfish may respond differently because food-web effects spread. A change can reach species people catch and eat.
scenes.caption: Watch the whole river, not one arrow. Blue catfish rise. Shared prey and shoreline habitat change. Crabs, small fish and white catfish may respond differently because food-web effects spread. A change can reach species people catch and eat.
scenes.visual: The BLUE bar rises while TEAL prey, TEAL crab and GOLD white-catfish bars move by different modest amounts; every bar says 'schematic'. Soft ripples travel along food arrows from the shared pool toward animals and then toward a person's fish basket. Keep uncertainty honest with 'may change' above the response bars.
scenes.narration: Watch the whole river, not one arrow. Blue catfish rise. Shared prey and shoreline habitat change. Crabs, small fish and white catfish may respond differently because food-web effects spread. A change can reach species people catch and eat.

scenes.tts: Human actions can help, too. People can restore habitat or remove some invasive fish. How far each population recovers is a question to test. A model lets us change one thing at a time.
scenes.caption: Human actions can help, too. People can restore habitat or remove some invasive fish. How far each population recovers is a question to test. A model lets us change one thing at a time.
scenes.visual: GREEN marsh blocks regrow along part of the bank while a few BLUE catfish move into a fishing boat. Response bars begin to move, then a large WHITE question mark covers them before they settle; never show how far any bar recovers. A WHITE loop arrow labelled 'test a model' cycles through one change at a time. Water and grass continue moving.
scenes.narration: Human actions can help, too. People can restore habitat or remove some invasive fish. How far each population recovers is a question to test. A model lets us change one thing at a time.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule to carry forward. When people change an ecosystem, populations may rise or fall. The rule guides predictions, but evidence must show what changed in a real river.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule to carry forward. When people change an ecosystem, populations may rise or fall. The rule guides predictions, but evidence must show what changed in a real river.
scenes.visual: Return to the widest river view. BLUE, GOLD and TEAL population bars settle at different heights, all labelled 'schematic'. A magnifying glass appears over the words 'real river evidence' as the scene prepares the handoff. The colour map remains visible in a small legend.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule to carry forward. When people change an ecosystem, populations may rise or fall. The rule guides predictions, but evidence must show what changed in a real river.

scenes.visual: Dim the moving river behind one centered line only: 'When people change an ecosystem, populations may rise or fall.' No title, logo, URL or smaller line appears.
